chapter: Joe Liggins and back to Kid Ory
title: Ory's changing pianists and trumpeters
summary: Barry and Joe run through the men who passed through Ory's band: Teddy Buckner, Gideon Honore, Lionel Rison, Lloyd Glenn and others, until Bob McCracken replaced Joe.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: So anyway, you stayed with Ory up until 1953. Blakeney was all the time in the band? Oh, no, Teddy
Darensbourg - 204
Buckner came in, didn't he.
Yes. Teddy was in the band then. Ram was still in the band, and what's his name was still playing...Honoré...
Gideon Honoré.
Gideon Honoré was playing piano in the band.
Oh, I didn't know he worked regularly with Ory.
Oh yeah. He was playing there when I left, and then Braud was playing bass.

Ory had such an unbelievable changeover of clarinet players, as we said before. But then he started changing everybody around. He had trumpet players, Blakeney and Teddy Buckner and Alvin Alcorn, Red Mack...
Right.
...played there a little while. And the same thing happened with piano players. He had Donohue after Buster died...
Right.
Who else did he have in there? Didn't L.Z. Cooper come back in there for a little while?
Yeah, he came back and played...
Darensbourg - 205
Yeah, that's right. Because he's on a thing, the tape I've got with Nick playing with Ory's band...
I think Vernel played with him for a little while.
Vernel...

And then they had another old boy, I can't think of his name... Vernel used to call him his brother. He looked something like Vernel. But he left there and went to Oregon. Maybe you'd recognize his name. But he was a good piano player. He looked something like Vernel. And I thought he was Vernel's brother for a while.
Oh, Lionel Rison(?)?
Yeah. Right.
I saw Lionel Rison(?) just two weeks ago, when I was in New Orleans.
He went back to New Orleans?
No, they're living somewhere out there. He's a preacher or something like that now, some revival...
I often wonder what happened to him.
Yeah, he lives in...
When I was in Oregon, ...(?)... in 1962 with Louis...
He's down there where them freejacks(?) and all that come from, down in the south peninsula thing... You
Darensbourg - 206
know, the freejacks(?)...
Out of New Orleans?
Yeah, out of New Orleans. Just a few miles away, 30-40 miles. But anyway, he was living out there. Lionel Rison. That's right, he did records with Ory, too.
He played with Ory, that's right. He was in the band. And Lloyd Glenn.

Lloyd Glenn, another one, yeah. So Ory seemed to me to have... The only really what you'd call 100 percent regular was Tudie and Ram -- Tudie and Ram and Ory. The rest of it was like a nucleus. But they stayed with him the whole time, didn't they.
Another guy was Freddie Washington. He had a piano player named Freddie Washington.
But Fred died, didn't he?
Yes. There's no end to the guys... Anyway, when I lift the band, a clarinet player, Bob McCracken(?), came in.
Oh, he replaced you.
